description: A value per category, as bars: the analytical card's second form after <Sparkline> (a value over time). Carries its own scale, grid, legend and hover readout, and reads as a table to a screen reader. Reach for <Meter> when there is one value against one target, and for a <Table> when the numbers are compared exactly rather than at a glance. Copy: category labels are the categories' own names, short enough to sit under a bar without turning. The accessible label says what is being counted and over what.

props.name: data
props.description: The columns, in the order they are read.

props.name: series
props.description: Names the measures in `values`. Two or more turn the chart into a grouped (or `stacked`) one and bring a legend with them.

props.name: stacked
props.description: Segments of one column instead of columns side by side: for parts of a whole per period. Only with `series`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Bars run across instead of up. The answer for long category names and for a ranking, where the eye compares lengths down a column of labels.

props.name: max
props.description: Top of the scale. Defaults to the first nice number above the data; pass it when several charts must share one scale.

props.name: target
props.description: A goal drawn across the columns, so a bar can be short OF something. Its own label is deliberately not a prop: a word printed inside the plot sits on the data (owner, 23.08). Name the goal in the card's meta line.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: The one column that carries the accent — the current period, the site under discussion. Single-series charts only; the others stay quiet.

props.name: axis
props.description: The scale down the side, and the grid lines with it. On by default: a bar with no scale is a shape, and the reader cannot say how big it is.

props.name: showValues
props.description: Values printed on every bar. Off by default — the readout under the pointer says it for the one bar being read, which is what a reader asks.

props.name: label
props.description: What the chart measures. Required in practice: it names the chart for a screen reader, which then reads the table this component renders for it.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP-47 tag for the numbers. Omit to follow the browser.

example:
<Grid columns={12} gap={4}>
  <GridItem span={8}>
    <Card>
      <Stack gap={3}>
        <SectionLabel as="h3">Over time</SectionLabel>
        
        <BarChart
          data={CLOSED}
          target={40}
          emphasis="Aug"
          tone="success"label="Findings closed per month"
        />
      </Stack>
    </Card>
  </GridItem>
  <GridItem span={4}>
    <Card>
      <Stack gap={3}>
        <SectionLabel as="h3">By team</SectionLabel>
        
        <BarChart
          data={BY_TEAM}
          orientation="horizontal"
          size="sm"
          tone="warning"
          label="Open findings by team"
        />
      </Stack>
    </Card>
  </GridItem>
</Grid>
